text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch finance ministry loses the theoretical right to influence monetary policies of the central bank DNB. (p1)
- Steel maker Hoogovens may opt for majority stake in Belgium's steel concern Boel after signing of 50-50 joint venture agreement last Friday. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank loses battle over pay and conditions agreement for its call centre staff. (p1)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm stuck in legal wrangling over publication of Dutch Securities Board STE inquiry into downfall of stockbrokers Nusse Brink. (p1)
- Electronics firm Getronics expects earnings per share to grow by 20 percent in the coming years. (p1)
- Temp agency Randstad grew faster than rivals in the sector last year. (p3)
- Van Dorp Groep which provides office supplies and medical disposables hires external bureau to investigate potential of the group's activities. (p4)
- Construction and dredging company Ballast Nedam closes lease deal with Britain's bank Morgan Grenfell to finance its dredger "Amsterdam". (p4)
VOLKSKRANT
- Regional Christian Democrats party leaders criticise chiefs and parliamentary representatives for loss in recent poll. (p1)
- ABN Amro bank employee steals four million guilders. (p2)
- Bank insurer ING's real estate arm ING Vastgoed and Korea's Samsung SAGR.CN to build 760 million guilders worth of office buildings in Warsaw, Poland. (p2)
- Engineering firm Heidemij HEIDF.AS sells remaining 5.6 percent stake in rival Fugro. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Industrial group Stork misses out on order for water treatment plant in Curacao. (p13)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Chemicals concern DSM to build its fourth dyneema-fibre plant in the U.S. or the Far East. (p11)
TROUW
- Surinam government furious about tightened drugs control at Amsterdam Schiphol Airport for flights from Paramaribo. (p1)
- Labour party PvdA slashes tax plans of Liberal social affairs junior minister Frank de Grave. (p2)
